::: {.callout-important appearance="simple"}
## Status: design. The pair-counting probe has not run. Not a protocol.

This is the strongest novelty claim of the set and the weakest on feasibility. Section 2
records the searches that establish the first; probe PA decides the second.
:::

## 1. The question

Meta-research tells other fields that a finding which does not replicate is not a finding. The
field publishes many studies measuring the same practices: reporting quality in a specialty,
data sharing in a set of journals, registration adherence in a trial population. Their samples
overlap. Nobody has asked whether they agree.

If two meta-research studies measuring the same practice over overlapping literature report
materially different rates, the field's own evidence base has the property it criticizes
elsewhere.

## 2. Novelty, with the searches that establish it

Claims of novelty in this project must show the search that produced them, because a
model-recalled absence of prior work is not evidence of absence.

**Corpus regex**, over 1830 tier A records and 7412 frame records, title and abstract:

```
(concordan|discordan|agreement|consisten).{0,50}between.{0,40}
(methodological review|meta-research|cross-sectional stud).{0,40}(same|identical)
|overlapping (methodological|meta-research)
```

**Result: 0 records.**

What does exist, and is the closest prior work, is PMID 37433624, a systematic review with
individual participant data meta-analysis of studies investigating data and code sharing. It
pools meta-research studies; it does not ask whether they agree with each other. That
distinction is the study.

This section is updated, not deleted, if review finds prior work the searches missed.

## 3. Hypothesis

Pairs of meta-research studies measuring the same practice in overlapping populations report
rates that differ by more than sampling error alone would produce.

**Primary null.** Between-study heterogeneity in the paired rate difference is consistent with
sampling variation.

**What would falsify it.** Heterogeneity consistent with chance, which would be a strong
positive result about the field and is the outcome the field would hope for.

## 4. Sample

The unit is a **pair**, and pairs are what the probe must count before anything else is
decided. Candidate pairs come from two places:

1. The included-study lists of meta-research syntheses already in the corpus. PMID 37433624 is
   the largest and its included studies are, by construction, meta-research studies measuring
   the same construct.
2. The corpus itself, matched on topic block plus the population studied, extracted from the
   abstract.

A pair qualifies when both studies measure the same practice, in the same discipline or journal
set, over overlapping publication years, and both report an extractable rate with a denominator.

## 5. Outcome

The absolute difference in reported rate between the two members of a pair, with each study's
own denominator, so that the expected difference under sampling variation alone is computable.

## 6. Analysis

In R. For each pair, the observed rate difference against the difference expected from the two
binomial denominators. Aggregated as an excess-heterogeneity statistic across pairs, with a
permutation null built by pairing studies that do **not** share a population.

The permutation null is the part that makes this a test rather than a description: without it,
any two rates differ and the result is unfalsifiable.

## 7. Threats, and what happened to each

| threat | what was done | removed or disclosed |
|---|---|---|
| "Same practice" is a judgment | Pair eligibility is adjudicated by the author against written criteria, not by a model | Disclosed |
| Overlapping samples are not identical samples | The expected difference accounts for denominators but not for which specific articles were sampled; partial overlap inflates apparent disagreement | Disclosed |
| Pairs may not exist in usable numbers | Probe PA counts them before anything else | Removed by the probe, or the study ends |
| Publication years differ, and practice changes | Pairs restricted to overlapping year ranges; year gap reported per pair | Disclosed |
| Reported rates use different denominators for the same word | Every rate is re-extracted with its denominator rather than taken from an abstract percentage | Removed |

## 8. Probes

| probe | computes | goes to | what would change the design | status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **PA** | candidate pairs from the included-study list of PMID 37433624 and from corpus matching | 4 | fewer than 10 usable pairs makes this an agenda item | outstanding |
| **PB** | how many candidate pairs have an extractable rate and denominator in both members | 5 | below about 20 the permutation null is not usable | outstanding, depends on PA |
| **PC** | author adjudication of "same practice" on the candidates | 4 | disagreement with the written criteria means the criteria are wrong, not the pairs | outstanding, needs the author |

## Deviations

Recorded on the result page: what changed, when, why, and the estimate before and after where
that can be computed. A deviation is not a failure; concealing one is.

## What this cannot show

- It cannot say which member of a disagreeing pair is right.
- It cannot separate genuine disagreement from different but equally defensible definitions of
  the same practice, which may be the most common cause of any disagreement found.
